title: fix(formula): a date field compared with addDays(today(), N), date() or timestamp() evaluates like the today() comparison

Skills-docs: none — `skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md` already lists `addDays`, `addMonths`, `date`, `datetime` and `timestamp` as returning a timestamp and never tells an author to avoid comparing one with a date field, so what it teaches now holds at run time as written

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：流程、校验规则或公式里拿日期字段和「30 天后」「下个月」这类算出来的日期比较时，现在按字面意思算；以前比大小每次运行都报错，比相等在正好那天也答「不相等」，流程被悄悄跳过。
- 为什么做：属于「表达式校验与作者护栏」，替编写流程的管理员和代写流程的 AI 助手解决「保存通过、运行时却不按预期执行」。
- 出错会怎样：已上线的流程里用了这种写法的，升级后会开始触发（发邮件、建记录等），这正是作者本来想要的；本改动可整体撤回。
- 要你做什么：无。

## What changes

A `date` field reaches a flow condition, a validation rule or a formula as its `YYYY-MM-DD` text. `celEngine.evaluate` converts that text when it meets a Timestamp, in two rewrites in `packages/formula/src/cel-engine.ts`:

- the ADR-0032 §1c retry (`rewriteFaultedOperands`, #1530 / #7098) for an ordering that faulted, which asks `operandKind` whether the other side is a Timestamp;
- the #3183 equality rewrite (`rewriteTemporalCallEquality`), which asks `isTemporalCall`.

Each kept its own hand list: `operandKind` knew `today` / `now` / `daysFromNow` / `daysAgo` plus `date` / `datetime`; `isTemporalCall` knew only the first four. The environment also declares `addDays`, `addMonths`, `addWorkingDays`, `addWorkingHours` and cel-js's `timestamp` as returning a Timestamp, and neither list had them. Measured on `origin/main` 5b8ca361 (`record.due_date = '2026-11-29'`, the day after the run):

| condition | before | after |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `record.due_date < addDays(today(), 30)` | faults: `no such overload` (the text against a `google.protobuf.Timestamp`) | `true` |
| `record.due_date < addMonths(today(), 1)`, `< addDays(record.borrow_date, 30)`, `< timestamp("2030-01-01T00:00:00Z")` | faults, same | evaluates |
| `record.due_date == addDays(today(), 1)` | **`false`**, no error | `true` |
| `record.due_date != addDays(today(), 1)` | **`true`**, no error | `false` |
| `record.due_date == date("2026-11-29")`, `== timestamp("2026-11-29T00:00:00Z")` | **`false`**, no error | `true` |
| `record.due_date == daysFromNow(1)` (control) | `true` | `true` |

Through the flow runtime (`AutomationEngine.execute`, start condition): the ordering returned `success: false` ("condition failed to evaluate as CEL"), and the equality returned `success: true, skipped: true` with the next node run 0 times. All three save doors accept every one of these spellings, before and after (readings in #37848's report).

The fix: one set, `timestampReturningFunctions()`, read once from `getDefinitions()` of an environment built by the same constructor the engine evaluates on (global functions whose every overload returns `google.protobuf.Timestamp`). `isTimestampCall` asks it, and both rewrites ask `isTimestampCall`. The two hand lists are gone, the equality rewrite's cheap source gate reads the same set, and a function registered later with a Timestamp return is covered by both rewrites with no edit. None of the three §1c conditions changes (an operator that faults on a mixed pair, a counterpart proven a Timestamp, an operand whose own value is ISO date text), and the equality arm still wraps only a field reference, per occurrence.

One existing pin moves, by the seat's ruling that the equality path also takes `date` / `datetime`: the #7168 idempotence case `date(record.due) == previous.due` now rewrites to `date(record.due) == date(previous.due)`. The coerced side is still never wrapped twice. A Date-valued `previous.due` passes through `date()` (still `true`); two ISO texts used to answer a silent `false` and now answer `true`. Null and non-date operands answer as before (measured on both trees: `false` for `==`, `true` for `!=`).

- `.changeset/38135-date-field-against-timestamp-call.md`: `minor` for `@objectstack/formula`, both declaration lines, and in plain words that deployed flows whose condition failed or was skipped start firing.

## Tests

- `packages/formula/src/cel-overload-retry-scope.test.ts`, new top-level describe: ordering against `addDays(today(), N)` (either side), `addMonths`, `addDays(record.borrowed, 14)`, `timestamp(…)`; answers equal the `daysFromNow(30)` spelling across the boundary days; a datetime field's instant meets `addDays(now(), 1)`; non-date text (`soon`, `7`) stays a fault.
- `packages/formula/src/cel-engine.test.ts`, new top-level describe: the rewrite wraps the field opposite `addDays` / `addMonths` / `date` / `datetime` / `timestamp`, and leaves `daysBetween(…) == 0`, `round(…)` and an already-coerced operand alone; `==` / `!=` answer what `daysFromNow(1)` answers on the day and the day before; a string literal beside it keeps its answer. **Drift pin**: enumerates every global Timestamp signature `getDefinitions()` declares, needs a probe row per name (a new function fails it until it has one), checks the set both rewrites ask equals it, and checks each function meets a field holding its own instant under `==`, `!=`, `<` and `<=` (working-day functions with a calendar).
- `packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-registration-schema-e2e.test.ts`, new top-level describe (kernel rig, `library_loan.due_date: date`, clock pinned): `record.due_date < addDays(today(), 30)`, `addDays(today(), 30) > record.due_date` and `record.due_date == addDays(today(), 1)` fire the next node exactly as their `daysFromNow` spellings do; a loan outside the bound is skipped, not failed; `registerFlow` accepts the spellings with no date advisory.
- Door controls, by the seat's ruling (the doors do not change): `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.test.ts` (`os validate`'s pass) has no finding for six spellings at start, edge and `decision` conditions; `packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-flow-condition-record-date-text.test.ts` (the publish door on the real `ObjectQL` rig) publishes three spellings and they go `active`.

## Acceptance notes

- `addWorkingDays` / `addWorkingHours` still fault in a flow condition for the reason they always did (no working calendar outside a formula or a stored field's `expression`); the drift pin exercises them with a calendar.
- The Skills-docs line is `none` (see the line's reason).

## Verification

Read first, by risk:
1. `packages/formula/src/cel-engine.ts`, `timestampReturningFunctions` / `isTimestampCall`, and the `operandKind` hunk: what counts as a Timestamp counterpart now.
2. The same file, `rewriteTemporalCallEquality`: the gate and the two wrap lines.
3. `packages/formula/src/cel-engine.test.ts`, the moved #7168 idempotence pin.

Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/formula exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/cel-engine.test.ts src/cel-overload-retry-scope.test.ts -t 38135` shows 14 passing tests.
